missed.why: A 3-axis Hall magnetometer, 16-bit X and Y, I2C. It is not a dedicated angle die. Firmware on the measurement coprocessor takes atan2(By, Bx) under a diametric magnet on the horn axis. Values: (a) Interface: I2C standard mode 100 kHz and fast mode 400 kHz; option -011 answers at address 00011xx = 0x0C to 0x0F, the last two bits strapped by A0 and A1; VDD 2.2 / 3 / 3.6 V min / nom / max; E code -40 to +85 degC (covers 0 to 50 degC). (b) Resolution: XY sensitivity 0.161 to 3.22 uT/LSB; Figure 2 plots XY noise on a 0 to 60 mGauss axis, so noise is at most 6 uT if the axis top is the worst case (curve values not read numerically). The 0.129 degree step (2.25 mrad) then holds at a field in the XY plane above about 2.7 mT; the magnet's field at the sensor is not stated, for this part or any other candidate. (c) Travel: the XY pair gives the full 360 degrees, so +/-90 degrees is inside it. (d) Update: Table 19 gives 1.27 ms (OSR 0, DIG_FILT 0) to 7.60 ms (OSR 1, DIG_FILT 4) for an XYZ conversion, inside the 50 ms poll. exclusions_not_holding.part: MLX90393 rows (and 3D magnetometers of the same kind)
exclusions_not_holding.reason_given: MLX90393 is a 3D magnetometer with no angle output; not read at JLCPCB
exclusions_not_holding.why_it_fails: V209 and V210 ask for a measured position at 0.129 degree or finer over 180 degrees, not for a dedicated rotary-sensor die. TMAG5273A2QDBVR, P2's rank 1, is itself a 3-axis Hall sensor whose angle is computed from X and Y, so 'no angle output' separates the two parts by where atan2 runs, not by a requirement value. The MLX90393 data sheet states 16-bit X and Y at 0.161 to 3.22 uT/LSB, and the part now reads at JLCPCB: C2654971 stock 2222, presale 2147 (2026-10-02T06:55:28Z), Digi-Key Active 28,268 (06:56:14Z).

exclusions_not_holding.reason_given: comparator delay: 80 ns maximum at 25 degC only (MCP6561), 20 ns maximum at TJ 25 degC only (LMV7219); not stated over 0 to 50 degC
exclusions_not_holding.why_it_fails: The clip's own comparator-delay value is under 21.8 us. 80 ns and 20 ns are 0.4 % and 0.1 % of it, so the missing 0 to 50 degC statement cannot change the result for the clip placement. The over-temperature maximum counts only where the part is the optical index's comparator, and P2 itself keeps TLV7011DBVR, TLV7031DBVR and TLV1811DBVR for the clip placement alone with no maximum stated at all. The two parts are excluded from the index placement only. Their other values (input range, supply, output, stock) were not re-read in this task.

exclusions_not_holding.part: BPV10NF, BPW34, VBPW34S and other PIN photodiodes (with an emitter on the probe board)
exclusions_not_holding.reason_given: sensor selected and working distance: a photodiode alone is not a reflective sensor, and no operating distance is stated
exclusions_not_holding.why_it_fails: This forks on a design choice for the owner. A probe board that carries an infrared emitter and a PIN photodiode, assembled by JLCPCB, is a reflective infrared sensor on a probe board (V219); P2's own readings give the detector times that meet the 1.244 us share (BPV10NF tr 80 ns, tf 60 ns; BPW34 100 ns) where all 9 integrated sensors fail it. The pair has no part-level 'stated operating range' (V220) because the range is a design output, computed from the emitter's stated radiant intensity and the photodiode's stated sensitivity; the pen line's reflectance and width are not stated, and TCND5000's 2 to 25 mm is likewise stated for a reference target, not the pen line. I did not select an emitter or compute the range, and no discrete pair is listed under missed for that reason. TCND5000's own drop holds: its data sheet (Rev 1.6, read 2026-10-02T06:52:01Z) states rise and fall times of 15 ns for the emitter only.
